content.comment_body: This solution did not work for me. I believe the issue is related to Java, as after installing [product_name] successfully, the application does not start and instead creates a dump file at C:\Users\xxxxx\AppData\Local\CrashDumps. The file generated is javaw.exe.10092.dmp. This occurs every time I try to launch [product_name]. Any suggestions? [user_name]
Please provide the dump file so we can take a closer look.
I have attached the file, but I am unable to open it. Regards,

It appears that the Windows 10 Creators Update (version 1703) causes some Java applications to malfunction. [product_name] works on Windows 10 Anniversary Update (version 1607) and previous updates before Creators Update (1703). Consider reverting to a restore point or backup prior to the 1703 update, or reinstall Windows 10 from a source older than version 1703, such as version 14393.0.161119-1705.rs1.... .esd. You can convert .esd to iso using ESD Decrypter for Windows 10 build 15063 and earlier versions (search online for this tool).
Hello. I experienced the same issue, and the solution was to delete the folder named "God Mode." See the following thread for more details: [url]
Confirmed—after deleting the "God Mode" folder, [product_name] launched without any issues. This problem occurs with Windows 10 version 1703.
A new question submitted by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled '[product_name] - crashing immediately on startup.' Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users have reported that [product_name] fails to launch on Windows 10 after the Creators Update (version 1703), leading to Java-related crashes and creation of dump files. This major compatibility issue is specific to Windows 10 version 1703; earlier versions do not exhibit the problem. Ultimately, users discovered that deleting the 'God Mode' folder resolves the issue, but this workaround is not intuitive and points to a significant usability challenge for Java-based [company_name] applications on updated Windows systems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to start and operate reliably on Windows 10, even after system updates. They also anticipate trouble-free usage without encountering technical difficulties stemming from components like Java.
